newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-SWAIN SPRINGS ASCOT SURPRISE IN KING GEORGE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SWAIN SPRINGS ASCOT SURPRISE IN KING GEORGE.

text.p: Swain, a 16-1 outsider ridden by John Reid, won the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Diamond Stakes on Saturday in a line-up rated by some as the best in decades.
Second place in the high class eight-strong field went to Pilsudski, partnered by Michael Kinane, with French raider Helissio, the mount of Cash Asmussen, third.
Swain took up the running with 300 metres to go to land the $489,000 first prize for the Godolphin outfit, brainchild of Sheikh Mohammed.
Pilsudski, Eclipse Stakes winner, was a 6-1 shot while Helissio, the 1996 winner of the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, started 11-10 favourite.
